answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. The result is a self-purifying economy: every epoch, low-cost fake identities are filtered out by the same reputation mechanics that reward the honest ones.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a quartz as the anchor of the cost.
